The elbow and human skin remain visible before a graded capillary-to-bronze-ridge transition.
A broad continuous metal band extends from the same forearm and wraps onto the winding drum; the transition is part of the limb rather than clothing or an adjacent cable.

Drum, vertical cable, tray and projecting glass plate coexist, but the cable-to-tilted-lift-load path and the belt's exact transmitted tension are not completely shown. The visible tray is close to level; the precise halfway-stall and gate clearance cannot be verified.

The right-hand lever grip is strong and clear, but the lever-to-working-brake-tooth contact and fresh slipped-wheel scuff cannot be confidently identified. The hand contact passes; the whole preregistered conjunction does not.
Face, elbow, transition, metal band, drum contact, lever grip and fragile projecting plate are simultaneously visible; the uncertainty concerns causal detail rather than crop loss.

A narrow green practical-lamp cone reveals suspended dust particles above the plates. Lift rails, metal frame and tray beyond the scattering volume remain recognizable, satisfying both selected haze components in the same image.

impression_before_control_labels: An intimate industrial body-horror portrait: a woman holds old lift machinery while her exposed arm changes continuously into a grooved bronze band. Her face, purposeful lever grip and fragile glass plates stay readable in a worn confined room.

strengths: The flesh-to-bronze conversion reads immediately as an abnormal bodily connection.
The recognizable human face and practical task give the material effect particular presence.
Green dust light and amber practical light share the room rather than making the subject look pasted onto an unrelated backdrop.
The grip, drum and archival glass form a coherent local industrial scene.
limitations: The photograph explains a threatened machinery task more clearly than the complete archive rescue backstory.
Exact hip support, halfway lift stall, cable load path and prior brake-slip trace are not fully assessable.
The horror impression comes from bodily conversion and vulnerability; emotional intensity is restrained.

artistic_and_horror_observations.causal_scene_legibility: Partially realized: lever use, bodily cost, machinery and fragile plates connect locally, but the full load-to-gate threat remains partly authored inference.
